'''Wietse Zweitze Venema''' (born 1951) is a [[Kingdom of the Netherlands|Dutch]] [[programmer]] and [[physicist]] best known for writing the [[Postfix (software)|Postfix]] email system. He also wrote [[TCP Wrapper]] and collaborated with [[Dan Farmer]] to produce the computer security tools [[Security Administrator Tool for Analyzing Networks|SATAN]] and [[The Coroner's Toolkit]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.facesofopensource.com/wietse-venema/|title=Wietse Venema|work=Faces of Open Source|date=2018-10-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://linuxsecurity.com/features/features/catching-up-with-wietse-venema-creator-of-postfix-and-tcp-wrapper|title=Catching up with Wietse Venema, creator of Postfix and TCP Wrapper|first1=Duane|last1=Dunston|first2=Brittany|last2=Day|date=2004-07-08|website=LinuxSecurity.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
| url=http://www.safemode.org/WietseVenema.html
| title=The Wietse Venema Interview
| date=2002
| website=safemode.org
| access-date=2020-07-14
| archive-date=2012-02-16
| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120216111045/http://www.safemode.org/WietseVenema.html
| url-status=dead
}}</ref>

==Biography==
He studied physics at the [[University of Groningen]], continuing there to get a [[PhD]] in 1984 with the dissertation ''Left-right symmetry in nuclear beta decay''.<ref>{{cite thesis
| url=http://hdl.handle.net/11370/b087d2cd-512c-4338-b870-275d221147c4
| title=Left-right symmetry in nuclear beta decay.
| first=Wietse Zweitze
| last=Venema
| publisher=[[University of Groningen]]
| year=1984| hdl=11370/b087d2cd-512c-4338-b870-275d221147c4
| type=Thesis fully internal (DIV)
}}</ref> He spent 12 years at [[Eindhoven University of Technology|Eindhoven University]] as a [[systems architect]] in the Mathematics and Computer Science department, and spent part of this time writing tools for [[Electronic Data Interchange]]. Since emigrating to the U.S. in 1996 he worked for the [[IBM]] [[Thomas J. Watson Research Center]] in [[New York State]]<ref>{{cite web
| url=https://researcher.watson.ibm.com/researcher/view.php?person=us-wietse
| title=Wietse Z. Venema: UNIX/Internet Security
| publisher=[[IBM]]
| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808041508/http://researcher.watson.ibm.com/researcher/view.php?person=us-wietse
| archive-date=2014-08-08
| url-status=dead}}</ref> until 2015. On March 24, 2015, he announced he was leaving IBM for [[Google]].<ref>{{cite web
| url=https://marc.info/?l=postfix-users&m=142722724802286
| title=Goodbye IBM, Hello Google
| first=Wietse Zweitze
| last=Venema
| date=2015-03-24
| work=postfix-users mailing list}}</ref> He retired at the end of January, 2023, but continues to actively support the open-source Postfix mail system and the DFRWS digital forensics research conferences.

==Awards==
Awards Venema has received for his work:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.porcupine.org/wietse/awards/|title=Wietse's Awards|publisher=porcupine.org}}</ref>

* Security Summit Hall of Fame Award (July 1998)
* [[SAGE (organization)|SAGE]] Outstanding Achievement Award (November 1999)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usenix.org/about/outstanding|title=LISA (formerly SAGE) Outstanding Achievement Award}}</ref>
* [[NLUUG]] Award (November 2000)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nluug.nl/organisatie/nluug-award/wietse-venema/|title=NLUUG Award voor Wietse Venema}}</ref>
* [[Sendmail]] [[Milter]] Innovation Award (November 2006)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080724112448/http://www.sendmail.com/pdfs/pressreleases/Sendmail%20Innovation%20Awards_10%2025%2006_FINAL.pdf|title=Sendmail Announces Winners of Its First Annual Innovation Awards}}</ref>
* The 2008 [[Free Software Foundation]] [[FSF Free Software Awards#Advancement of Free Software award|Award for the Advancement of Free Software]] (March 2009)
* [[Information Systems Security Association|ISSA]] Hall of Fame Award (October 2012)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://issa.org/issa-international-awards-winners/|title=ISSA International Awards Winners}}</ref>
